bar: There is no nameable bar. EDGAR shows no Scribe Therapeutics filing between the 2026-09-02 10-Q/8-K and 2026-09-22 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001853921.json, confirmed against https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001853921), and no issuer press release since 2026-09-02 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/SCTX/). positioning_check: FINRA short interest at the 2026-08-31 settlement: 778,191 shares, 2.63 days to cover on 295,438 ADV, up 173.3% from the 08-14 settlement of 284,711 (https://api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/SCTX/short-interest?assetclass=stocks, settlement 2026-08-31, published with FINRA's ~8-business-day lag so the position carried INTO the fall is not observable). Float: the 424B4 shows 17,577,386 shares out after the offering and 18,864,386 with the option fully exercised, which was fully exercised, plus a concurrent Sanofi private placement; the public float from the 8,580,000-share base plus the 1,287,000-share option is about 9.87m shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1853921/000119312526316503/d21355d424b4.htm, 2026-07-27). So shorts are roughly 8% of float at 2.6 days to cover against a 528k-share drop-day volume — small, coverable inside one session, and NOT squeeze fuel. There is no option chain at all (baseline: no_options_market), so there is no skew to read and no option-implied forward move; that removes the one place the market states a direction out loud.

findings.finding: The cause is genuinely absent from the primary record: no SEC filing between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-22, no issuer press release since 2026-09-02, and no analyst action, peer readout or short report found — so the seller has no name, no size and no end date.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name's only two comparable falls (2026-08-13 -11.47%, 2026-08-25 -16.21%) both rose the next close (+1.77%, +1.57%), but both sit inside a six-week post-IPO tape in which the sector was rising, and n=2 on a two-month trading record is the thinnest possible reaction function.
findings.why_not_priced: The price has already fallen 15% on whatever this is. What the move cannot reflect is the SHAPE of the seller: a dated, mechanical supply event (offering, index deletion, lock-up) is over on a known day and the market prices the end of it, and there is no such document here. If the fall had been a completed one-off the volume spike would look like a flush — 8x or more with a closing-range recovery — and instead it is 2.75x with the whole loss taken intraday and no gap, which is the signature of a continuing participant rather than a single print.
findings.independence: The company's own newsroom independently shows the same gap — nothing between the 2026-09-02 Q2 release and 2026-09-22: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/SCTX/

findings.finding: This is the third sharp idiosyncratic down day in under three weeks (-5.7% on 2026-09-03, -7.6% on 2026-09-16, -15.0% on 2026-09-21) in a ~9.9m-share float two-month-old IPO, while the biotech complex moved about -1% — a distribution pattern, not a single event.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The prior two of these (the 08-13 and 08-25 falls in the baseline's history block) each bounced ~1.6-1.8% the next close, but the sequence since has been lower highs: the stock is at 0.482 of its 52-week range having traded to $39.60, and each successive fall has been larger.
findings.why_not_priced: Each individual day is priced; what is not in the 09-21 close is that a seller working a ~9.9m-share float over three weeks has, on the evidence of the two prior episodes, not finished after one session. If the market believed the supply was exhausted, the 2.75x volume day would have closed off its low and the next-day open would be gapping up, and a 12%-ATR name with a cleared overhang usually reprices in one session rather than three.
findings.independence: A separate outlet records the 2026-09-03 episode at -5.7% from the same source family but a different publication date: https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/09/04/scribe-therapeutics-nasdaqsctx-trading-down-5-7-should-you-sell.html

findings.finding: ARK Investment Management bought about 67,740 SCTX shares (~$1.9m, implying ~$28.05 — the drop-day close) for ARKG on the drop day itself, roughly 13% of the session's $14.8m of dollar volume, and ARK's trade file only publishes after the close, so the 09-21 print could not contain it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior ARK accumulation in this name is on the record — SCTX has only traded since 2026-07-23 — so this is a first add and ARK's pattern in newly added names is to build over consecutive sessions rather than in one print. Treated as a weak prior, not a measured reaction function.
findings.why_not_priced: ARK publishes its daily trades after 16:00 ET on the trade date, so no part of the 09-21 close reflects the disclosure — only the anonymous buying pressure inside the tape. What the price did not get is the signalling half: a visible, followed buyer initiating into a 15% fall. If it had been priced, the drop-day close would have printed well off its low rather than at -15.0% with the whole loss intraday.
findings.independence: A second outlet reports the same ARK/ARKG add in SCTX from an independent feed: https://www.benzinga.com/etfs/sector-etfs/26/09/61923369/cathie-wood-loads-up-on-biotech-5-etfs-holding-her-latest-bets

findings.finding: The commonest second-leg-down mechanism is structurally unavailable: the baseline's EDGAR text probe returns zero hits ever for "at-the-market", the company reported ~$43.0m cash at 30 June plus ~$140.6m of IPO and private-placement net proceeds with runway into 1H 2029, and as a July 2026 IPO it is not Form S-3 eligible and is inside a 180-day lock-up, so no shelf, ATM or follow-on can sell into the next session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's going-concern probe hits six times, all on pre-IPO S-1 and 424B4 documents describing the pre-money state (most recent 2026-07-27); nothing post-IPO carries it, and the 2026-09-02 10-Q did not reinstate it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is broadly priced — a well-funded biotech does not trade on its runway. The part the 15% print does not reflect is that the fall itself cannot force a financing, which is the mechanism that turns a one-day fall into a five-day fall in most microcap biotech. If the market feared dilution here the fall would have gapped rather than bled intraday, and the 2.75x volume would have been far heavier.
findings.independence: The baseline's own EDGAR full-text probe returns hits_ever = 0 for "at-the-market" across every Scribe filing: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001853921.json

outside_window.finding: STX-1150 Phase 1 first-in-human data in elevated LDL-C is guided to 1H 2027; the registry entry gives primary completion 2028-12-30. This is the entire equity story and none of it resolves inside this window.
The IPO lock-up expires 180 days after 2026-07-23, i.e. around 2027-01-19, releasing roughly 10m insider shares against a ~9.9m public float. A dated supply event, far outside this window.
